questions.question: Describe Hitler's early career up to 1924 and explain the main ideas he set out in Mein Kampf.
questions.expected_answer: Born in Austria in 1889, he failed as an art student in Vienna, absorbed nationalism and antisemitism, served in the German army in World War I and believed the stab-in-the-back myth. He joined the German Workers' Party in Munich in 1919, which became the NSDAP in 1920, and led it from 1921. After the failed Beer Hall Putsch of November 1923 he was tried, sentenced to five years and served about nine months, writing Mein Kampf: a false racial hierarchy with Aryans at the top and Jews as enemies, lebensraum in eastern Europe, destruction of Versailles, crushing communism and a single all-powerful leader.

questions.question: Explain how the Wall Street Crash of 1929 led to the Great Depression and why Germany was hit especially hard.
questions.expected_answer: Over-speculation in shares ended in a collapse of prices in October 1929; banks failed, savings were lost, spending and production fell and unemployment rose. Tariffs reduced world trade and American banks recalled foreign loans. Germany's recovery since 1924 depended on American loans; when they were recalled, businesses and banks collapsed, industrial production fell by about 40 percent and unemployment reached about 6 million by early 1932.

questions.question: Explain how the Depression changed German politics between 1930 and 1932 and why the Nazis gained support.
questions.expected_answer: The coalition government collapsed in 1930 and Brüning governed by Article 48 decrees, cutting spending, which weakened parliamentary democracy and deepened hardship. Voters turned to extremes: the Nazis rose from 2,6 percent in 1928 to 18,3 percent in 1930 and the Communists also grew. The Nazis promised work, bread, order and national pride, used powerful propaganda and blamed Jews and communists as scapegoats, appealing to the middle class, farmers, the young and those fearing communism.
